naming: The loader deserializes with YamlDotNet's CamelCaseNamingConvention and refuses any key it does not know.

keys.description: Optional grouping label (the source system) the platform files the flow's pipeline and runs under. A blank value counts as none.
What a test takes when it says nothing itself.
The most failing records an assertion names, 1 to 500. Counts are always exact; the examples are the first ones met.

How long, in seconds (0 to 3600), the search index is given to list a change before a test of the changed type is judged: a run within that time of a delivery, removal or restore this module made to records of a test's entity type skips the test, saying what changed and from when a run judges it. 0 judges every test whatever changed.
The most records a test reads, 1 to 1,000,000. A test whose query matches more is not evaluated over its records (its count and grouping still are), unless it sets `sample: true`.
`storage` reads each record as storage holds it, found by the search; `index` reads the search hits themselves, which hold only what the index keeps.
Optional text describing what the tests check.

Which outcomes fail the platform run: `error` fails it on a test that failed an error-severity assertion or could not be evaluated; `warning` on a warning-severity failure as well; `never` reports and succeeds. A failed run still records its report, and notifications fire on it as on any failed run.

The document kind: `assertion`, qualified tests of what an OSDU partition holds, run after the flows that populate it. The loader chooses the reader by it and refuses a document that declares no `flowType` or `documentType`.

The assertion flow's name: its pipeline identity, and the name its reports are kept under. A flow that tests partitions keeps a report per partition, shown as `name@partition`. Named `<source>-<type>-<counter>-<area>-assertion`, so it sorts after the flows it tests.

Optional: the flow's parameters, by name. `{name}` tokens are usable in a test's `query`, its `ids` and the text an assertion compares with (never in a `matches` expression); `{partition}` is always the partition the run tests, so no parameter may be called `partition`. Values come from `--set name=value`, the run's values, or the schedule's `values`.
One parameter; `<name>` is the name its `{name}` tokens use. A run supplying a value for a name the flow does not declare is refused.
The value used when a run supplies none.
Text describing what the parameter is for.
When true, a run that supplies no value, for a parameter without a default, fails with "parameter 'name' is required". A scheduled fire supplies only the schedule's `values`, so give it one there.

The OSDU data partitions the flow tests, hard-coded: each by its `data-partition-id` written literally, never a reference, at least one, at most 64, none twice. A run tests one of them: the one it names, else the registry's default when the flow names it, else the flow's only one; `*` is refused, since a report describes one partition. Left out, with no `data-partition-id` header, the flow tests every registered partition. Each partition keeps a report of its own.
One partition the flow tests, by its `data-partition-id`.

The HTTP settings (timeout, retry, rate limit, TLS, URL allowlist and response size), and `concurrency`: the tests evaluated at once, and the requests each has in flight. `reliability.parallelInterfaces` is refused.
A delivery flow's setting: rendered documents per work batch file. The loader accepts it as on a delivery flow; an assertion flow does not use it.
A delivery flow's setting: records claimed per ledger round trip when retrying records. The loader accepts it as on a delivery flow; an assertion flow does not use it.
The tests evaluated at once, and the requests (storage reads, reference lookups, bulk reads) one test has in flight. At least 1.
A delivery flow's setting: the member runs a large submission spreads over. The loader accepts it as on a delivery flow; an assertion flow does not use it.
A delivery flow's setting: below this many records a submission never fans out. The loader accepts it as on a delivery flow; an assertion flow does not use it.
A delivery flow's setting: how long a worker's lease on a record lasts. The loader accepts it as on a delivery flow; an assertion flow does not use it.
A delivery flow's setting: the target's declared request body ceiling (0 = not declared). The loader accepts it as on a delivery flow; an assertion flow does not use it.
The largest response body read, in bytes. A larger response fails the request with a message naming this setting.
A delivery source's setting: how many of its interfaces run at once. An assertion flow runs no interfaces, so the loader refuses it here.
The most requests per second the flow sends to the platform; 0 means unlimited. Token requests are not limited.

A delivery flow's setting: renderers in the intake pipeline on one node, 0 to 256 (0 takes half the machine's processors, at least one). The loader accepts it as on a delivery flow; an assertion flow does not use it.
How one request is repeated inline. Only requests that are safe to repeat are repeated, on 408, 425, 429, 503 and 504 and on a transport failure; 500 and 502 are not replayed.
The most attempts one request gets, the first included.
The wait between attempts: `exponential` doubles `baseDelayMs` per attempt, `fixed` waits `baseDelayMs` each time; both are capped at `maxDelayMs`.
The first wait between attempts, in milliseconds.

Whether a `Retry-After` the service sends is honoured. A requested wait within `maxDelayMs` becomes the floor of the backoff; a longer one is never shortened, so the request stops instead of waiting it out.
The longest wait between attempts, in milliseconds.
A delivery flow's setting: the first wait between a record's attempts across worker passes, in minutes. The loader accepts it as on a delivery flow; an assertion flow does not use it.
A delivery flow's setting: the longest wait between a record's attempts across worker passes, in minutes. The loader accepts it as on a delivery flow; an assertion flow does not use it.
A delivery flow's setting: statuses that hold a record instead of retrying it. The loader accepts it as on a delivery flow; an assertion flow does not use it.
One HTTP status code.
How long one HTTP request may take, in seconds.

The hosts requests may reach (an SSRF guard), checked on every request and every redirect hop. Empty allows any host the deployment's network policy reaches; token requests are not checked against it.
A host name, or `*.suffix` to match the bare domain and any subdomain of it. Compared ignoring case.
Whether the platform's TLS certificate is verified. `false` also needs `SQLFLOW_DELIVERY_ALLOW_INSECURE_TLS=true` on the node, or the run is refused.
The OSDU platform the tests read, and where its services are served. Tests only read: nothing is ever written to OSDU.

How requests to the OSDU platform authenticate, written as `target.auth` is on a delivery flow. Secrets are references only: ${env:NAME} or ${keyvault:vault/secret}. Left out, requests carry no credentials (type `none`).
keys.appliesWhen: Optional; written as `target.auth` on a delivery flow.

keys.description: The header an `apiKeyHeader` auth sends the key in.
keys.appliesWhen: source.auth.type is apiKeyHeader, which needs it.

keys.description: The secondary secret, as a reference (${env:NAME} or ${keyvault:vault/secret}): the username for `basic`, the client id for `oauth2ClientCredentials` (sent as `client_id` unless the token body names one).

The primary secret, as a reference (${env:NAME} or ${keyvault:vault/secret}), never a literal: the token for `bearer`, the key for `apiKeyHeader`, the password for `basic`, the client secret for `oauth2ClientCredentials` (sent as `client_secret` unless the token body names one).
keys.appliesWhen: Needed by bearer, apiKeyHeader and basic; used by oauth2ClientCredentials.

keys.description: The OAuth2 token endpoint: where a token is requested and how it is read from the answer. One token serves the run and is requested again shortly before it expires.
keys.appliesWhen: source.auth.type is oauth2ClientCredentials, which needs it.

keys.description: The text put before the access token in the `Authorization` header.
When true, the client id and secret are sent as an HTTP Basic `Authorization` header on the token request instead of in its form body.

Extra form fields of the token request, by name. `grant_type` is `client_credentials` unless set here, and `client_id` and `client_secret` come from `secondarySecretRef` and `secretRef` unless set here.
One form field of the token request; `<name>` is the field name (such as `scope`). The value may be a reference (${env:NAME} or ${keyvault:vault/secret}), resolved before the request is sent.
An OIDC discovery document whose `token_endpoint` is the token URL. When set it is used instead of `url`; it may be a reference.
keys.appliesWhen: source.auth.type is oauth2ClientCredentials; give this or url.

keys.description: The path of the access token in the token endpoint's JSON answer.
The token endpoint URL, usually a reference such as `${env:OSDU_TOKEN_URL}`.
keys.appliesWhen: source.auth.type is oauth2ClientCredentials; give this or discoveryUrl.

keys.description: The auth scheme: `none`, `bearer` (a token as a reference), `apiKeyHeader` (a key in a named header), `basic` (username and password) or `oauth2ClientCredentials` (a token requested from `token`). Read ignoring case.
The text put before the secret in the header value of a `bearer` or `apiKeyHeader` auth. An OAuth2 token takes `token.applyPrefix` instead.
Where the Wellbore DDMS is served under the platform, for a test that reads bulk data (`/ddms/v3/{collection}/{id}/data`).
The base URL of the OSDU platform, usually a reference such as `${env:OSDU_URL}`, the same one the delivery flows it tests deliver to.

Headers sent with every request. A flow that names its partitions, or tests every registered one, may not name `data-partition-id` here: each run sets it to the partition it tests. A flow that names neither tests the partition this header names.
One header; `<name>` is the header name (`data-partition-id: dev`). A value may be a reference (${env:NAME} or ${keyvault:vault/secret}).
The legal service's root, under which `/legaltags:validate` answers whether a legal tag is valid.
The search service's offset search, which counts, groups and asks how records were indexed (openapi search v2, POST /query).
The storage service's read by id, of records a test reads whole and of references it looks up (openapi storage v2, POST /query/records).
The search service's cursor search, which a test pages through the records it reads (openapi search v2, POST /query_with_cursor).
The tests, 1 to 500, each reading one OSDU kind and holding what it reads to its assertions. A run runs every test, or those its payload names by test or tag.
One test: what it reads (a kind found by a query, or records named by id, and optionally their bulk data) and the assertions it holds that to.
The assertions, 1 to 100. Each names one subject: count, field, column, aggregate, unique, groupBy, recordSet, conforms, indexed, legal, delivered, rowCount, columns or monotonic.
One assertion: exactly one subject, the keys that subject takes, and optionally a name, a description and a severity. A key the subject does not take is refused, naming it.
Groups that must not appear at all.
One group's value.

An aggregate of the values of `field` over every record read, or of `column` over each record's rows, compared with the comparison keys beside it (`equals`, `atLeast`, ...) within `tolerance`. `count` counts values, `distinct` distinct values, `missing` records (or rows) without one; min and max also take dates.
This value or more: a number, or a date and time.
This value or less.
Between two values, both included: `[low, high]`, both numbers or both dates.
One value: text, a number, or true or false.
A column (curve) of each record's bulk data. With one operator it is a column assertion, held for the share of each record's rows `for` asks; with `aggregate` or `monotonic` their measure.
The columns each record's bulk data holds.
The columns every record's bulk data has, and no other, in any order.
One column.
Columns no record's bulk data may have.
One column.
Columns every record's bulk data has.
One column.
true: every record meets the template of its kind: the properties it requires, and the type, format, pattern, enumeration and ranges of every value. Needs `read: storage`.
A list holding this value, or text holding this text.

How many records the test matches (the index's exact count, or the ids storage holds): a whole number (equals), or a mapping of `equals`, `notEquals`, `atLeast`, `atMost`, `greaterThan`, `lessThan` and `between`, every one of which has to hold.
This number or more.
This number or less.
Between these two numbers, both included: `[low, high]`.
Equal to this number.
More than this number.
Less than this number.
Not equal to this number.
A delivery flow: every record its ledger holds as delivered in the partition is among the records the test matches. What a delivery says it sent is so held to what OSDU holds.
Why the assertion matters, as reports show it.
Whether the value is empty (null, empty text, an empty list or object), or not.
Text ending with this.
Equal to this value: a number as a number (within `tolerance`), text as text (and as an instant when both are ISO 8601 dates), true or false. Text holding a number equals the number.
With delivered: the test matches no record the ledger does not hold either.
Whether there is a value at all (true), or none (false).

A path into each record, from a root property (`data.FacilityName`, `acl.viewers`, `legal.legaltags`, `tags.RunMarker`): arrays are crossed implicitly, or with `[*]` and `[n]`. Checked against the template of the test's kind before anything is read. With one operator it is a field assertion; with `aggregate` its measure.

The share of records (or of each record's rows, for a column) the condition has to hold for: `all`, `any`, `none`, or a percentage such as `95%`. With none considered, all, any and a share fail and none passes.
More than this value.
Groups the records the test matches by the distinct values of this field, as the search's `aggregateBy` answers it over the whole index: nothing is read, so any number of records is grouped.
How many groups there are: a whole number (equals), or a mapping of `equals`, `notEquals`, `atLeast`, `atMost`, `greaterThan`, `lessThan` and `between`, every one of which has to hold.
This number or more.
This number or less.
Between these two numbers, both included: `[low, high]`.
Equal to this number.
More than this number.
Less than this number.
Not equal to this number.
The groups expected, each with what its count has to be.
One group's count: a whole number (equals) or a comparison. `<name>` is the group's value.
This number or more.
This number or less.
Between these two numbers, both included: `[low, high]`.
Equal to this number.
More than this number.
Less than this number.
Not equal to this number.
Compares text ignoring case: for equals, in, matches, startsWith, endsWith and contains.
One of these values, 1 to 1000.
One value: text, a number, or true or false.

true: the search indexed every record the test matches cleanly: none carries an index status other than 200 (a mapping or conversion failure, a missing schema). The failing examples carry the indexer's trace.
The interface of the delivery flow whose ledger is read, for a source delivering several.
`valid`: every legal tag the records carry is valid now, as the legal service answers it (`/legaltags:validate`); a record with none fails too.
What the length of text or of a list has to be: a whole number, or a comparison.
This number or more.
This number or less.
Between these two numbers, both included: `[low, high]`.
Equal to this number.
More than this number.
Less than this number.
Not equal to this number.
Less than this value.
Matches this .NET regular expression, taken as written (no tokens); a match taking longer than a second fails the value.
`includes`: the groups listed are there with their counts, others allowed. `exact`: they are the only groups there are.
The order `column`'s values keep row after row in each record's bulk data, as an index curve does; absent values are passed over. The failing example names the two rows that break it.
keys.appliesWhen: With column; the test reads bulk data.

keys.description: What reports call the assertion; left out, a label read off what it asserts. At most 200 characters.
A list not holding this value, or text not holding this text.
Not equal to this value.
None of these values.
One value: text, a number, or true or false.
Does not match this regular expression.
Passes over a record (or row) with no value at all, instead of failing it.

The records projected onto `columns` and compared as a set of rows with `rows`, as DeltaForge's RESULT SET is. Values compare exactly as JSON: 5 and "5" differ; a field with no value is null, and one with several the list of them.
The fields each record is projected onto, 1 to 20.
One field.
`exact`: the same rows in any order. `ordered`: the same rows in the test's `sort` order. `includes`: these rows are there, others allowed. `excludes`: none of these rows is there.
The rows expected, at most 1000, each a list with a value per column.
One row: a value per column, in column order.
One value: text, a number, true or false, or null for no value.

true: every value is a reference to a record storage holds. An entity type (`master-data--Well`): to a record of it. Looked up a hundred at a time once the records are read; the failing examples name the dangling references.

How many rows each record's bulk data holds: a whole number (equals), or a mapping of `equals`, `notEquals`, `atLeast`, `atMost`, `greaterThan`, `lessThan` and `between`, every one of which has to hold.
This number or more.
This number or less.
Between these two numbers, both included: `[low, high]`.
Equal to this number.
More than this number.
Less than this number.
Not equal to this number.
How much its failure matters: an error fails the test, a warning warns, an info is reported.
Text starting with this.
How far a number may be from the value compared with and still be equal to it, or within a range.
The JSON type the value has to be; an integer is a number without a fractional part.
Fields whose values, taken together, no two records may share (1 to 20). Records holding none of them are passed over.
One field.
For a path yielding several values in one record: `all` holds the record when every value meets the condition, `any` when one does.
Conditions selecting the records (or rows) the assertion looks at, 1 to 10, every one of which has to hold; each on a field (a column, for a column assertion) with one operator.
One condition: a field or column and one operator; it holds when one of the values meets it.
Selects the records (or rows) whose value this value or more: a number, or a date and time.
Selects the records (or rows) whose value this value or less.
Selects the records (or rows) whose value between two values, both included: `[low, high]`, both numbers or both dates.
One value: text, a number, or true or false.
The column of the row the condition reads.
Selects the records (or rows) whose value a list holding this value, or text holding this text.
Selects the records (or rows) whose value whether the value is empty (null, empty text, an empty list or object), or not.
Selects the records (or rows) whose value text ending with this.

Selects the records (or rows) whose value equal to this value: a number as a number (within `tolerance`), text as text (and as an instant when both are ISO 8601 dates), true or false. Text holding a number equals the number.
Selects the records (or rows) whose value whether there is a value at all (true), or none (false).
The path into the record the condition reads.
Selects the records (or rows) whose value more than this value.
Compares text ignoring case: for equals, in, matches, startsWith, endsWith and contains.
Selects the records (or rows) whose value one of these values, 1 to 1000.
One value: text, a number, or true or false.
Selects the records (or rows) whose value what the length of text or of a list has to be: a whole number, or a comparison.
Selects the records (or rows) whose value less than this value.
Selects the records (or rows) whose value matches this .NET regular expression, taken as written (no tokens); a match taking longer than a second fails the value.
Selects the records (or rows) whose value a list not holding this value, or text not holding this text.
Selects the records (or rows) whose value not equal to this value.
Selects the records (or rows) whose value none of these values.
One value: text, a number, or true or false.
Selects the records (or rows) whose value does not match this regular expression.

Selects the records (or rows) whose value true: every value is a reference to a record storage holds. An entity type (`master-data--Well`): to a record of it. Looked up a hundred at a time once the records are read; the failing examples name the dangling references.
Selects the records (or rows) whose value text starting with this.
How far a number may be from the value compared with and still be equal to it, or within a range.
Selects the records (or rows) whose value the JSON type the value has to be; an integer is a number without a fractional part.

Read each record's bulk data from the Wellbore DDMS, for rowCount, columns, column and monotonic assertions. The kind must be one the DDMS keeps bulk data for (a WellLog, a WellboreTrajectory, a PPFGDataset, a WellPressureTestRawMeasurement).
The columns (curves) read; left out, those the assertions name.
One column, as the DDMS names it; no commas.
The most rows read of one record's bulk data, 1 to 100,000,000. A record holding more fails the assertions over its rows, unless the test samples.
What the test checks, as reports and the board show it.
Records the test reads by id instead of searching, 1 to 1000, with tokens (`{partition}:master-data--Wellbore:123`). An id storage does not hold is left out of the count and named.
keys.appliesWhen: Not beside query, spatial or sort.

keys.description: One record id.

How long, in seconds (0 to 3600), the search index is given to list a change to records of this test's entity type before the test is judged; within it the test is skipped with the reason. 0 judges it whatever changed.

The one type the test reads, in one version: `authority:source:entityType:major.minor.patch`, as the `template.kind` of the mapping that delivers it names it. A kind with wildcards is refused, since a test is checked against one schema and reads one type in lineage.
The most records the test reads, 1 to 1,000,000.

The test's name, unique in the flow (ignoring case): a letter or digit followed by letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-`, at most 100 characters. A run names a test by it, and its history is kept under it.
The partitions of the flow the test runs in, when not all of them. A run in another partition records the test as skipped.
keys.appliesWhen: Not on a flow whose partition is its header's.

keys.description: One partition the test runs in.
A Lucene query narrowing the kind (`data.Source:"Recall"`), with `{parameter}` and `{partition}` tokens. Leading wildcards are refused by the search service.
Where the test reads the records its assertions look at: storage (every property, exactly as stored) or the search hits (only what the index holds). `conforms` needs storage.

When more records match than `maxRecords`: false (the default) evaluates none of the assertions over the records and says so, since the rest could fail them; true evaluates the first `maxRecords` and marks the result a sample.
The severity of the test's assertions that state none. An error that fails fails the test; a warning makes it warned; an info is reported and changes nothing.
The order the search returns records in, 1 to 5 fields; what an ordered record set compares against.
One field the search sorts by.
The field, as the index names it.
Ascending or descending.

A spatial filter the search applies (openapi search v2, `spatialFilter`): a geo `field` and exactly one of `byBoundingBox`, `byDistance`, `byGeoPolygon`, `byIntersection`, `byWithinPolygon`, each point a `{ latitude, longitude }`.
Records within a box: `{ topLeft: { latitude, longitude }, bottomRight: { latitude, longitude } }`.
Records within `distance` metres of `point`.
Records within a polygon: `{ points: [...] }`.
Records intersecting polygons: `{ polygons: [{ points: [...] }] }`.
Records within a polygon: `{ points: [...] }`.
The geo field the filter applies to, such as `data.SpatialLocation.Wgs84Coordinates`.
Labels a run selects tests by (the payload's `tags`) and the board groups and filters them by; at most 20.
One tag, written as a test name is.

The saved template version the test's fields are checked against: the mapping's `template.version`, so the test is checked against the schema the mapping renders to; left out, the newest saved for the kind. A test that reads fields of a kind with no saved template is not evaluated, and says how to capture one.
